summary: Why opening a connection takes three messages and not two.

steps.say: Two machines that have never spoken. Neither knows where the other will start counting bytes.
The client picks a starting sequence number x and sends it. This is a proposal, not a connection.
The server acknowledges x and proposes its own starting number y. One message doing two jobs.
The client acknowledges y. Now both sides know their own number arrived.

Here is the part people get wrong: the third message is not a formality. Without it the server has no proof its own sequence number was received — so an old delayed SYN could open a connection nobody asked for.
steps.aside: Two messages would leave the server guessing.
